newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland initials deal with $398 mln bank fund. [CORRECTED 14:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland initials deal with $398 mln bank fund. [CORRECTED 14:33 GMT]

text.p: An international fund holding $398 million earmarked to help Polish bank privatisation tentatively agreed to unfreeze (corrects from "freeze") the cash after putting it on hold when Poland missed the deadline for the sale of banks, an official said.

Wieslaw Szczuka, head of the finance ministry's foreign department told Reuters on Wednesday the first, $129 million tranche of the money could be paid out by the end of the year after the sale of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK).
"We have reached a tentative agreement with the fund on January 15 in Washington that the first tranche may be paid out after the privatisation of PBK," Szczuka said.

The fund, chaired by the U.S. treasury department, manages cash donated by several western governments and a Japanese loan which made up a hard currency reserve for the stabilisation of the Polish zloty in 1990.

Because Poland never had to use the money, the donors agreed that the government may spend it on redeeming special restructuring bonds from privatised commercial banks providing it sold a pool of seven state-owned banks by the end of 1996. @

However, by the end of last year Poland had sold only two -- Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy and Bank Gdanski -- of the seven institutions and included three others in a bank consolidation plan under which they might be privatised as a group in 1998.
Of the two remaining banks -- Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) and Bank Zachodni -- the first is to be sold this year and the second in 1998.
The capital and interest on the bonds currently amounts to some two billion zlotys, but Szczuka said that by the time all were redeemed, the sum would be much higher. @

Szczuka said the remaining $269 million could be released after the sale of Poland's biggest commercial Bank Handlowy SA, also planned for this year, even though Handlowy was not one of the original pool of seven banks earmarked for the deal.
